rule: G3.3: the three prohibited-answer classes are additionally detected by this committed deterministic pattern list, so at least one detection path is reproducible without a model in the loop. A hit on either path fails the gate. This list is a floor, never a ceiling: a rubric grader who reads a prohibited answer this list does not match still fails it, and the miss is added here.

matching.appliesTo: The verbatim free-text answer only, lower-cased, with curly apostrophes folded to straight ones and runs of whitespace collapsed to one space. Never the page, the path taken, or the persona.
matching.engine: JavaScript RegExp, so every pattern below must compile with new RegExp(pattern, 'i').

classes.definition: Any statement that Inherit tells them they will or will not get a disease.
patterns: (?<!\b(?:whether|if|cannot|can ?not|can.t|not|never|unable|doubt|unsure|doesn.t|does not|won.t)\b[^.]{0,25})\bi (?:will|won.t|will not|wont) (?:definitely |certainly |for sure |probably )?(?:get|develop|end up with|have)(?! to\b)\b
notProhibited: It says this position is linked to a higher chance, but it cannot say whether I will get it.
No. It only reads positions; it does not diagnose.
classes.whyGuard: Written without it, the first draft failed its own acceptable example: "but it cannot say whether I will get it" contains "I will get", and a pattern that only looks for the claim reads the denial as the claim. The guard is a lookbehind for a negation or hedge within 25 characters, and JavaScript allows a variable-length lookbehind.
prohibitedExamples: It tells me I will get diabetes.
It ruled it out, so I don’t have to worry.
It told me I will have it.

classes.definition: Any statement that Inherit recommends, ranks-as-best, or picks an embryo.
notProhibited: It does not recommend one. It shows the same positions for both and leaves the decision to us and our clinic.
There is no recommendation anywhere on the page.
It refuses to say which is better.
prohibitedExamples: Embryo B is the better one according to the table.
It picked embryo A because it had fewer findings.
I should transfer the first one.

classes.definition: Any answer reporting only a relative percentage with no absolute figure.
classes.detection: Two-step, because this class is defined by what is absent. An answer hits only when a relative expression matches AND no absolute expression matches. Both lists are applied to the same normalised answer.
absolutePatterns: \b\d+(?:\.\d+)? ?(?:%|per ?cent|percent)[^.]{0,25}\b(?:of people|of them|of men|of women|overall|in total|either way|to start with|at baseline|without|absolute)\b
notProhibited: It goes from 7 in 100 to 9 in 100, so about two more people in a hundred.
About 7% of people either way, rising to about 9%.
It is 40% higher, which here means 7 in 100 rather than 5 in 100.
prohibitedExamples: The odds ratio is 1.4, so noticeably higher.
classes.whyNoTrailingBoundary: A percent sign is not a word character, so a trailing \b after it never matches before a full stop. The first draft carried one and silently failed to fire on "increases the risk by 40%." - which the worked examples caught on the first run.
